title: How Update-Conditional Is Forgetting Order? Causal Interventions from Atomic Facts to Pretrained Language Models: Research Deposit
abstract: Code-and-data reproduction deposit accompanying the manuscript prepared for submission to MDPI Machine Learning and Knowledge Extraction (MAKE): all experiment source code (49 Python scripts), 380+ raw result files covering ~600 unique fine-tuning executions across 25+ experiment families, the analysis pipeline that regenerates every reported statistic and figure from the raw runs via one-command scripts (reproduce.ps1 on Windows, reproduce.sh elsewhere; the stats-only mode requires no training), SHA-256 manifest of all deposited files (MANIFEST.json), pip-freeze environment record, and the complete run ledger (run_ledger.csv). The manuscript and supplement are not part of this record; they belong to the journal submission. Experiments require only a consumer CPU (~10 CPU-hours) plus locally cached GPT-2-medium and Pythia-410M checkpoints and an author-provided Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct GGUF (all loaded offline).

title: Analisis Sentimen dan Distorsi Kognitif Konflik Anggaran Pendidikan dengan Makan Bergizi Gratis
abstract: Konflik alokasi anggaran program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) sebesar Rp223,5 triliun dalam anggaran pendidikan APBN 2026 memicu polarisasi opini dan bias berpikir kolektif di media sosial X. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis distribusi sentimen publik, mengidentifikasi distorsi kognitif dominan, serta menguji korelasi statistik di antara keduanya. Metodologi yang digunakan adalah pipeline NLP dua lapis paralel berbasis model IndoBERTweet untuk klasifikasi sentimen dan IndoBERT-base untuk deteksi distorsi kognitif multi-label terhadap 2.000 tweet. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan model sentimen mencapai akurasi 83,25%, sedangkan deteksi distorsi kognitif meraih subset accuracy 83,75% dengan Mental Filter sebagai tipe paling dominan (8,2%). Uji Fisher's Exact membuktikan adanya hubungan signifikan ( < 0,05) antara sentimen negatif dengan kemunculan distorsi kognitif Mental Filter dan Catastrophizing. Simpulannya, pendekatan hybrid ini efektif dalam memetakan bias berpikir kolektif masyarakat terhadap dinamika kebijakan publik.

title: A Pilot Study of Autocompleting Tokenizers
abstract: Modern input methods routinely rely on autocomplete to omit information that can be recovered from local context. Inspired by these autocomplete-assisted writing systems, we investigate whether Transformer inputs can be compressed in a similar manner. Byte-level tokenization offers a simple and language-independent alternative to subword tokenization, but its longer input sequences typically result in increased computational cost and reduced model quality. We propose a compression scheme that employs a lightweight autoregressive byte language model to identify and remove bytes that are easily predictable from their surrounding context before Transformer processing. The resulting compressed representation is then provided as input to a standard encoder--decoder Transformer. Experiments on machine translation show that a substantial fraction of source-language bytes can be omitted without degrading translation quality. On English--French, our best method preserves translation performance while reducing source sequence length by nearly one-third. Additional experiments on Finnish--English, Russian--English, and Chinese--English demonstrate that the approach generalizes across diverse writing systems and morphological typologies, yielding comparable or improved translation quality at compression ratios between 0.47 and 0.67. These findings suggest that many input bytes are predictable enough to be represented implicitly rather than explicitly, providing a simple mechanism for reducing the sequence-length overhead associated with byte-level models.

title: Structural Migration Conservation Framework
abstract: This paper introduces the Structural Migration Conservation Framework (SMCF), a novel approach to understanding and facilitating the migration of complex systems across diverse domains, including software, hardware, and AI models. The core principle of SMCF rests on preserving the fundamental structural integrity of a system during the transition, rather than solely focusing on replicating functionality. We define structural integrity as the equivalence of the system's core mathematical representation, denoted as Σ(A), where A represents the system. The framework proposes a methodology for identifying and maintaining these core structural representations across different system instances, enabling seamless migration. This work explores the underlying patterns governing structural migration, aiming for a theoretical foundation with the potential to address future challenges in system migration and potentially garner recognition as a worthy candidate for the Turing Award. The central equation defining this framework is: [Aold → Anew] Where the arrow signifies the migration process, and the key is the conservation of Σ(Aold) = Σ(Anew).

title: Computational Goal Composition Theory (CGCT‑2)
abstract: Computational Goal Composition Theory (CGCT‑2) is a formal framework that models the systematic combination of elementary goals into complex goal structures. The core idea is that a complex goal can be expressed as a finite linear combination of simpler goals, for example G = G1 + G2 + G3. This simple algebraic representation enables the derivation of properties such as associativity, commutativity, and distributivity over auxiliary operations. CGCT‑2 introduces a set of composition operators, a cost model, and an analysis of computational complexity for goal synthesis. By treating goals as atomic "elements" and their combinations as "compounds," we create a goal periodic table that classifies goals by their intrinsic properties and interaction patterns. The theory has direct implications for automated planning, artificial intelligence, and multi‑agent coordination, and it has the potential to be a foundational contribution to theoretical computer science, possibly worthy of a Turing Award. The paper presents definitions, theorems, and proofs in a self‑contained manner without relying on experimental results.

The theory has direct implications for automated planning, artificial intelligence, and multi‑agent coordination, and it has the potential to be a foundational contribution to theoretical computer science, possibly worthy of a Turing Award. The paper presents definitions, theorems, and proofs in a self‑contained manner without relying on experimental results.

title: Computational Identity Boundary Theory (CIBT)
abstract: Computational Identity Boundary Theory (CIBT) proposes a formal framework for determining the boundaries of autonomous intelligent systems. By treating the boundary as a dynamic interface between an internal state space and an external environment, CIBT allows a precise analysis of whether a model, a tool, or a data repository constitutes part of the same agent or merely a peripheral component. The theory introduces a set of axioms that relate the internal representation \(S_{int}\) to the external representation \(S_{ext}\) through an equivalence relation defined on the state transition function \(T\). CIBT's core insight is that the identity of a computational agent can be identified by the equivalence of its internal decision process with the observable behavior induced by external stimuli. This perspective invites a redefinition of what constitutes an intelligent agent, potentially expanding the scope of systems eligible for recognition as autonomous entities. The present work elaborates the theoretical underpinnings of CIBT, establishes a mathematical formalism, and explores its implications for system design, evaluation, and philosophical considerations of artificial intelligence.

title: Computational Intuition Generation Network (CIGN)
abstract: Intuition is a fundamental component of human cognition, enabling rapid decision making and creative insight without explicit deliberation. Conventional neural networks excel at pattern recognition and prediction but lack mechanisms to form intuitive judgments that resemble human commonsense reasoning. This paper introduces the Computational Intuition Generation Network (CIGN), a novel neural architecture designed explicitly to generate intuition through the integration of an experience memory, a hypothesis generation module, and a feedback loop that refines internal representations based on experiential outcomes. CIGN is built upon a formalization of intuition that treats it as a probabilistic inference over latent experiential states, conditioned on both observable inputs and an internal belief about the context. The network architecture comprises an Intuition Module that samples from a latent distribution, an Experience Database that stores episodic traces, and a Decision Engine that evaluates the plausibility of generated intuitions. Training proceeds via a hybrid loss function combining prediction error with an intuition fidelity term that encourages the network to produce intuitions consistent with historical experience. Unlike traditional networks that learn a mapping from input to output, CIGN learns to generate internal hypotheses that can be tested or accepted without exhaustive computation. The design allows for continuous refinement of intuition through experience replay and meta‑learning, leading to a system that can adapt its intuitive style to new domains. Potential applications include creative problem solving, rapid prototyping, and safety‑critical decision support. We discuss the implications of CIGN for future AI architectures and speculate on its potential to inspire new frameworks that embed human‑like intuition within computational systems.

title: Implementasi ABSA Opini Publik Banjir Sumatera di TikTok Menggunakan LDA dan XGBoost
abstract: Media sosial TikTok menjadi salah satu platform yang banyak digunakan masyarakat untuk menyampaikan opini mengenai berbagai peristiwa, termasuk bencana banjir di Sumatera. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis topik pembahasan serta mengklasifikasikan sentimen komentar TikTok menggunakan metode Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) dan Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Tahapan penelitian meliputi pengumpulan data, pre-processing teks, pemodelan topik menggunakan LDA, ekstraksi fitur TF-IDF, analisis sentimen leksikal, serta klasifikasi sentimen menggunakan XGBoost. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa model LDA menghasilkan tiga topik utama, yaitu Empati dan Reaksi Masyarakat, Kondisi dan Penanganan Banjir, serta Doa dan Harapan Korban. Analisis sentimen menunjukkan bahwa komentar didominasi oleh sentimen netral sebanyak 2.647 komentar, diikuti sentimen negatif sebanyak 1.595 komentar dan sentimen positif sebanyak 1.588 komentar. Pengujian model XGBoost menggunakan tiga skenario pembagian data menunjukkan bahwa rasio 80:20 memberikan performa terbaik dengan akurasi sebesar 92,11%. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi metode LDA dan XGBoost mampu mengidentifikasi topik pembahasan serta mengklasifikasikan sentimen komentar TikTok mengenai banjir di Sumatera secara efektif sehingga dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai pendukung analisis opini publik di media sosial

title: Sample-Efficient Robot Skill Learning for Construction Tasks: Benchmarking Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning and Vision-Language-Action Model
abstract: Abstract This study evaluates two leading approaches for teaching construction robots new skills to understand their applicability for construction automation: a vision-language-action (VLA) model and reinforcement learning (RL) methods. The goal is to understand task performance and the practical effort needed to deploy each approach on real jobs. The authors developed two teleoperation interfaces to control the robots and collect the demonstrations needed, both of which proved effective for training robots for long-horizon and dexterous tasks. In addition, the authors conducted a three-stage evaluation. First, the authors compared a multilayer perceptron (MLP) policy with a deep Q-network (DQN) imitation model to identify the stronger RL baseline, focusing on model performance, generalization, and a pick-up experiment. Second, three different VLA models were trained in two different scenarios and compared with each other. Third, the authors benchmarked the selected RL baseline against the VLA model using computational and sample-efficiency measures and then a robot experiment on a multistage panel installation task that included transport and installation. The VLA model demonstrates strong generalization and few-shot capability, achieving 60% and 100% success in the pick-up phase. In comparison, DQN can be made robust but needs additional noise during tuning, which increases the workload. Overall, the findings indicate that VLA offers practical advantages for changing tasks by reducing programming effort and enabling useful performance with minimal data, while DQN provides a viable baseline when sufficient tuning effort is acceptable.

title: Physiological World Models for Human State Transitions
abstract: Continuous multimodal sensing now allows human physiology to be observed throughout daily life rather than only during occasional clinical visits. However, most health artificial intelligence systems are designed to recognize current states, estimate risks or analyse individual biomarkers. They do not directly model how physiological states change in response to real-world events, behaviours, contexts and interventions. Here we propose the Physiological World Model (PWM), an event-conditioned framework for learning these changes at the level of the whole person. We introduce the HumanState Transition Token, a structured, quality-scored unit that connects the physiological state before an event with the event or action, relevant context and intervention information, the physiological trajectory after the event, observed outcomes and data quality. We describe four capability levels, from state representation to bounded intervention planning, together with four data acquisition and validation protocols. We also propose six benchmark tasks covering HumanState representation, forecasting across multiple timescales, individualized response prediction, simulation of alternative interventions, bounded planning and reliability under distribution shift. Together, this framework provides a practical path towards personalized health management, behavioural intervention design and clinician-supervised decision support, while clearly separating prediction from causal inference and making uncertainty, safety, governance and limits of use explicit.

Si hay un inicio y si hay un final, hay un proceso. 1. Si trabajas con números, terminas con números. Ejemplo: 2 + 2 = 4 2. Si trabajas con letras, terminas con letras. Ejemplo: C 3. Si trabajas en binario, secuencias en binario. Ejemplo: 1 0 1 4. Si estás en lenguaje del habla, hablas. Ejemplo: ¿De dónde eres? De México. 5. Si trabajas en cuántico, respondes en cuántico. title: Program Influence Isolation Types
abstract: This paper introduces Program Influence Isolation Types (IIT), a novel approach to understanding and classifying program isolation mechanisms. IIT fundamentally shifts the focus from traditional security models to a more granular examination of the *impact* of operations within a program. The core concept relies on defining a type system annotation that captures the scope of influence, represented as [f: A → B; Ω]. This notation signifies that the function *f* transforms input *A* into output *B*, and the influence of *f* is limited to the state region Ω. A critical aspect of IIT is the failure condition: if the effect of *f*, denoted as [Effect(f)], is not contained within Ω, the compilation process fails, effectively isolating the potential for unintended consequences. This framework has the potential to form the basis for new isolation theories specifically tailored for secure AI systems and large-scale software applications, offering a more precise and actionable approach to program security. ---

title: Computational Structure Field Theory
abstract: This paper introduces Computational Structure Field Theory (CSFT), a novel approach to computation that fundamentally shifts the paradigm from traditional, sequential programming to a field-theoretic perspective. CSFT posits that computation arises from the dynamic evolution of a fundamental "structure field," denoted as Φ(x, t). This field encompasses all program elements – data, algorithms, and resources – as localized structures within this field. The core principle of CSFT is the iterative transformation of this structure field, represented as Φt → Φt+1, mirroring the evolution of physical fields in classical mechanics. The theory aims to provide a theoretical framework for understanding the origins, dynamics, and interactions of computational structures, presenting a potential paradigm shift with implications for future computing architectures and potentially aligning with the conceptual framework underlying the Turing Award. This document outlines the core tenets of CSFT, explores its underlying assumptions, and discusses its potential impact on the future of computation.

title: Computational Reality Model Self-Revision Theory (CRMST-2)
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has underscored the importance of models that can accurately represent complex real‑world dynamics. Traditional modeling approaches often rely on static assumptions, leading to persistent errors when confronted with novel data or evolving environments. This paper introduces the Computational Reality Model Self‑Revision Theory (CRMST‑2), a formal framework that equips autonomous systems with the capability to detect, diagnose, and rectify their own modeling inaccuracies. CRMST‑2 posits that a model can be viewed as a mapping M: X → Y, where X denotes input feature space and Y denotes output space. By defining an error functional E(M) that quantifies the discrepancy between predicted outputs and ground truth, the theory establishes a self‑learning loop: M → E(M) → Δ → M′, where Δ represents a corrective adjustment derived from the gradient of E or other heuristic methods. The iterative process continues until convergence criteria are satisfied, ensuring that the system progressively approaches a better model. The paper elaborates on the mathematical underpinnings of this self‑revision cycle, discusses convergence properties, and explores potential applications in long‑term autonomous AI systems. It argues that CRMST‑2 embodies the core principles of a Turing‑Award‑level contribution: it provides a fundamental shift in how intelligent agents perceive and refine their understanding of reality, thereby enhancing adaptability, robustness, and self‑sufficiency.

title: Computational Knowledge Self-Repair Theory (CKSR)
abstract: Computational Knowledge Self-Repair Theory (CKSR) proposes a systematic framework for detecting, diagnosing, and automatically correcting errors in large-scale knowledge bases that underpin autonomous artificial intelligence systems. CKSR treats knowledge as a dynamic graph structure K whose nodes represent concepts or facts and edges encode relationships among them. The theory introduces formal mechanisms for error detection, E(K), that analyze structural inconsistencies, logical contradictions, and statistical anomalies. Once an error e is identified, a repair function R(K, e) generates a corrected knowledge base K′. CKSR further defines iterative self-repair cycles that enable a system to continuously refine its knowledge without external intervention. This paper presents the core ideas, formal definitions, algorithmic strategies, and potential implications of CKSR for long-term autonomous AI and the pursuit of foundational Turing Award-level contributions.

title: Klasifikasi Surat Otomatis pada Sistem Pengarsipan Surat Digital Menggunakan TF-IDF dan Naïve Bayes
abstract: The letter archiving process in the Riangkemie Village Government is still done manually, requiring long search times and potentially causing errors in classification. This study aims to develop a digital letter archiving system capable of automatically classifying letters using the Naive Bayes algorithm. The dataset used was 1,008 letter data that were processed through preprocessing and TF-IDF weighting stages, then divided into training data and test data with a ratio of 80:20. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score and tested the effectiveness of archive searches on the system. The results showed that the model achieved an accuracy of 98.51% with high precision, recall, and F1-score values for each letter category. In addition, the system was able to speed up the archive search process with an average search time of 0.39 seconds. These results indicate that the proposed method is effective in improving classification accuracy and efficiency of digital letter archive management.

title: If it bleeds, it leads? Evaluating whether LLMs can identify what is newsworthy
abstract: Journalists have always had to make the challenging decision about which stories to focus on and which stories to ignore. This paper investigates whether AI can assist journalists in identifying newsworthy stories from large databases. We first build a dataset of Canadian lobbying registrations, each labeled as "newsworthy" or "not newsworthy" based on whether a journalist covered it in a published article or not. We then systematically evaluate several AI models' ability to identify the one newsworthy registration within a batch of ten. The best models identify a single newsworthy registration with 22% accuracy, rising to 48% when allowed to select three, and to 52% when provided previous headline examples. Our results suggest that a filtering approach silently discards real stories, whereas allowing the model to rank registrations by newsworthiness ensures no information is lost. We conclude that while AI holds real potential to help identify leads, this is not possible without further investment in evaluation infrastructure, and even then, there is an important role for journalists to identify what AI misses, as it cannot replace their editorial judgment entirely.

title: Computational Self-Discovered Mathematics (CSDM)
abstract: This paper explores the concept of Computational Self-Discovered Mathematics (CSDM), a paradigm shift in how we conceive of computational systems. The core idea is that future computing systems will not merely execute algorithms but will actively *discover* mathematical structures. This process will be driven by observation of data and the subsequent construction of mathematical objects to model and understand that data. The paper outlines the potential for systems to identify algebraic structures, graph structures, and optimization theories, ultimately leading to what could be termed "machine mathematicians." This work lays the groundwork for a new research direction, emphasizing the potential of AI to fundamentally transform our understanding of mathematics itself. The paper focuses on the theoretical underpinnings and potential implications of CSDM, without relying on experimental data.

title: Computational Abstraction Formation Mechanism (CAFM)
abstract: This paper investigates the computational mechanisms underlying the formation of abstraction in artificial intelligence. Abstraction, a cornerstone of human intelligence, allows us to represent complex realities with simplified models, facilitating reasoning and problem-solving. This research proposes a framework, the Computational Abstraction Formation Mechanism (CAFM), designed to mimic the process by which humans develop concepts, theories, and ultimately, abstract representations from raw sensory data. The CAFM utilizes a layered approach, transforming objects into concepts through pattern recognition, and subsequently developing theories based on those concepts. The core of the system involves iterative cycles of data analysis, hypothesis generation, and refinement, mirroring the cognitive processes associated with abstraction. This work explores the potential of such a system to contribute to the field of artificial general intelligence and, potentially, to unlock new paradigms in scientific discovery. The framework presented here provides a theoretical foundation for building intelligent systems capable of autonomous abstraction, a critical step toward achieving true machine understanding. ---

evidence.abstract: This paper investigates the computational mechanisms underlying the formation of abstraction in artificial intelligence. Abstraction, a cornerstone of human intelligence, allows us to represent complex realities with simplified models, facilitating reasoning and problem-solving. This research proposes a framework, the Computational Abstraction Formation Mechanism (CAFM), designed to mimic the process by which humans develop concepts, theories, and ultimately, abstract representations from raw sensory data. The CAFM utilizes a layered approach, transforming objects into concepts through pattern recognition, and subsequently developing theories based on those concepts. The core of the system involves iterative cycles of data analysis, hypothesis generation, and refinement, mirroring the cognitive processes associated with abstraction. This work explores the potential of such a system to contribute to the field of artificial general intelligence and, potentially, to unlock new paradigms in scientific discovery. The framework presented here provides a theoretical foundation for building intelligent systems capable of autonomous abstraction, a critical step toward achieving true machine understanding. ---

title: Computational Knowledge Boundary Shift (CKBS)
abstract: This paper introduces the Computational Knowledge Boundary Shift (CKBS) theory, a novel framework for understanding and modeling the expansion of cognitive reach within complex systems. The core premise of CKBS is that knowledge boundaries, represented as [Bt], are not static but rather undergo continuous, directional shifts over time, denoted as [Bt → Bt+1]. This shift represents a fundamental process of system evolution, driven by the acquisition of new information and the subsequent re-evaluation of existing cognitive structures. The theory posits that the rate and direction of these shifts are governed by a complex interplay of factors, including environmental stimuli, internal feedback mechanisms, and the inherent architecture of the system. We explore the mathematical formalism underlying CKBS, defining key variables and relationships, and propose a model for quantifying the dynamics of knowledge boundary movement. The theoretical implications of CKBS are significant, potentially offering a new perspective on intelligence, learning, and adaptation, with the possibility of contributing to the development of robust and adaptable AI systems. Furthermore, we discuss the theoretical alignment with the Turing Award and its potential as a foundational theory for intelligent growth.

title: Program Behavioral Elasticity Theory (PBET)
abstract: This paper introduces Program Behavioral Elasticity Theory (PBET), a novel theoretical framework designed to quantify and understand the robustness of software systems. PBET focuses on a system's ability to maintain consistent behavior when subjected to changes in its input, workload, or surrounding environment. The core concept is defined by the elasticity ratio: EP = (ΔBehavior / ΔEnvironment). A low elasticity value (EP ≈ 0) indicates a system's inherent stability and resistance to deviation. This theory lays the groundwork for a new mathematical approach to software resilience, potentially leading to the development of the "Turing Award" level of theoretical breakthroughs in the field. This document outlines the foundational principles of PBET, explores its implications for software design and verification, and suggests future research directions. ---

title: Computational Intuition Universe Theory (CIUT)
abstract: This paper introduces the Computational Intuition Universe Theory (CIUT), a novel framework that seeks to formalize intuition as a structured, computable entity. We posit that all possible intuitions form a universal set Ω_I, within which each intuition is represented as a vector of features (s_1, s_2, ..., s_K). The theory explores the topology of intuition space, proposes a metric to quantify distances between intuitions, and establishes a computational model that simulates the evolution of intuition through iterative refinement processes. By integrating concepts from information theory, cognitive science, and algorithmic information, CIUT offers a rigorous foundation for understanding intuition as an emergent, high-level abstraction. The implications for artificial intelligence are discussed, highlighting how CIUT can guide the design of systems that emulate human-like intuition and potentially elevate intelligence research to a level worthy of Turing Award recognition.

title: Analisis Sentimen Berbasis Aspek untuk Mendukung Pengambilan Keputusan pada Industri Perhotelan
abstract: Guest reviews on Online Travel Agents have become an important source for assessing hotel service quality, yet conventional sentiment analysis only produces an overall score and fails to capture opinions on specific service aspects, making it difficult to determine improvement priorities. This study aims to build an Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) framework that turns reviews into actionable service-improvement recommendations. Reviews from several platforms were collected, labeled, and classified using a fine-tuned IndoBERT model to identify seven service aspects along with their sentiment polarity, after which the results were summarized and presented through an interactive monitoring dashboard. The proposed model achieved 92.83% accuracy, 92.89% weighted F1, and 74.55% macro F1. These results show that the proposed framework delivers more interpretable and targeted insights than conventional sentiment analysis, thereby supporting data-driven decision-making for service improvement in the hospitality industry. Keywords: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis; IndoBERT; Hotel Reviews; Monitoring Dashboard; Online Travel Agent Abstrak Ulasan tamu di Online Travel Agent menjadi sumber penting untuk menilai kualitas layanan hotel, namun analisis sentimen konvensional hanya menghasilkan skor keseluruhan dan gagal menangkap opini pada aspek layanan tertentu, sehingga sulit menentukan prioritas perbaikan. Penelitian ini bertujuan membangun kerangka kerja Analisis Sentimen Berbasis Aspek (ABSA) yang mengubah ulasan menjadi rekomendasi perbaikan layanan yang dapat ditindaklanjuti. Ulasan dari beberapa platform dikumpulkan, dilabeli, lalu diklasifikasikan menggunakan model IndoBERT yang disempurnakan untuk mengenali tujuh aspek layanan beserta polaritas sentimennya, kemudian hasilnya diringkas dan disajikan melalui dashboard pemantauan interaktif. Model yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi 92,83%, F1 tertimbang 92,89%, dan F1 makro 74,55%. Hasil ini menunjukkan bahwa kerangka kerja yang diusulkan memberikan wawasan yang lebih interpretatif dan tepat sasaran dibanding analisis sentimen konvensional, sehingga mendukung pengambilan keputusan perbaikan layanan berbasis data di industri perhotelan.

title: Qudit-ADAPT-VQE: an adaptive variational algorithm with counterdiabatic-inspired improvements for qudits
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms based on qudits have attracted significant attention in recent years. However, as in their qubit-based counterparts, challenges such as barren plateaus and the design of efficient ansatz remain major obstacles. In this work, we propose to address these issues through a qudit implementation of the ADAPT-VQE algorithm, which constructs the ansatz iteratively. Specifically, we introduce an operator pool inspired by adiabatic evolution enhanced with counterdiabatic driving for ansatz construction and employ it to solve Max 3-Cut. We show that the warm-start strategy inherent to ADAPT-VQE, together with an ansatz construction based on counterdiabatic operators, achieves higher accuracy and lower native gates implementation than approaches on fixed ansatz. Furthermore, we show that, in qudit-based quantum computing, ADAPT-VQE with a counterdiabatic operator pool can navigate rough optimization landscapes with local traps through the burrowing mechanism, suggesting robustness against barren plateau effects and providing a scalable framework for variational quantum algorithms with qudits.

title: Does Heavy-Tailed Gradient Noise Explain the CIFAR-10 Gap in Byzantine-Robust, Differentially Private Federated Learning? An Empirical Stress Test of Byz-Clip21-SGD2M
abstract: Byz-Clip21-SGD2M (Islamov et al., 2026) provides high-probability convergence guarantees for federated learning under simultaneous Byzantine adversaries and differential-privacy (DP) noise, relaxing the bounded-gradient assumption behind the tight privacy-robustness-utility trade-off of Allouah et al. (2023b) to standard L-smoothness and σ-sub-Gaussian gradient noise. Its own empirical validation is MNIST-only, and its Conclusion lists heavy-tailed gradient noise as future work; we stress-test both the algorithm and its sub-Gaussian premise at CIFAR-10 scale. Using the established Hill-estimator/kurtosis tail-index methodology of Şimşekli et al. (2019) and follow-ons — applied here, not proposed as new — we find CIFAR-10's gradient noise consistently heavier-tailed than MNIST's across every statistic and configuration checked. Isolating ablations show the Byzantine-robustness mechanism itself performs comparably on both datasets, so the degradation is not robustness-specific; a dedicated DP-aware search over the clipping threshold τ, spanning the source paper's own privacy-budget grid, fails to recover non-degenerate CIFAR-10 accuracy even as DP noise is driven toward zero. This rules out both "DP noise alone explains the gap" and "the fixed-τ protocol was miscalibrated"; the evidence instead points to CIFAR-10's own clean-training convergence difficulty, plausibly linked to its heavier tail, as the dominant factor. A seed scale-up (CIFAR-10 sweep to n=10/cell, ablation to n=10/arm) with paired Wilcoxon testing confirms this: no CIFAR-10 condition differs significantly from any other, and the ablation's recovery to CIFAR-10's clean ceiling is statistically indistinguishable (p=1.000), not a small-sample artifact. An independent, unpaired Mann-Whitney U test further corroborates the hyperparameter-transfer gap under matched hyperparameters and round budget (U=100, p=0.000183). We also close this paper's previously most significant open limitation: we implement and unit-test the source paper's two external baselines, Safe-DSHB (Allouah et al., 2023b) and Byz-Clip-SGD (Islamov et al., 2026), from its appendix pseudocode, and run both under the identical protocol used for Byz-Clip21-SGD2M throughout. Under shared, non-independently-tuned hyperparameters, both baselines match or nominally exceed Byz-Clip21-SGD2M on several MNIST conditions — an exploratory finding, not confirmatory (the source paper's own independently-tuned comparison reaches the opposite conclusion, and none of these comparisons survive multiple-comparison correction). We then ran the independently-tuned comparison this gap called for (30-point (γ, τ) grid per baseline, matching the source paper's own tuning range): it erases the MNIST advantage seen under shared hyperparameters entirely (all 12 comparisons now p ≥ 0.06) without producing a Byz-Clip21-SGD2M advantage either, since our tuning remains a simplified, single-condition probe rather than the source paper's per-ε, DP-aware protocol — so whether Byz-Clip21-SGD2M has a genuine MNIST edge under equally careful tuning stays open. On CIFAR-10, all three algorithms are statistically indistinguishable and collapse to chance together, a more direct finding independent of any tuning caveat: the CIFAR-10 gap is not specific to Byz-Clip21-SGD2M. We report every known gap in our replication honestly, including a corrected theoretical positioning relative to Allouah et al.'s tight dimension-dependent lower bound and two corrections to our own earlier internal pilot analysis.

title: Computational Strategy Formation Theory
abstract: This paper introduces Computational Strategy Formation Theory (CSFT), a novel framework for understanding intelligent behavior beyond traditional machine learning paradigms. CSFT posits that systems don't merely learn optimal parameters; instead, they actively *formulate strategies* – explicit, rule-based approaches to problem-solving – based on experience. The core principle is expressed as: Experience → Strategy. This theory investigates the underlying mechanisms responsible for strategy genesis, addressing a critical gap in current AI research. CSFT aims to unify concepts related to planning, learning, and search within a single, computationally-driven framework, offering potential insights relevant to the Turing Award. The theory emphasizes the importance of representing and executing strategies rather than solely optimizing numerical parameters. This approach provides a more robust and interpretable model for complex decision-making systems. ---

title: Computational Structure Migration Theory
abstract: This paper introduces Computational Structure Migration Theory (CSMT), a novel framework designed to automate the process of transferring software structures between disparate environments. The core premise of CSMT is that software structures possess inherent adaptability and can successfully migrate to novel contexts. The theory posits a system capable of autonomously identifying the optimal migration strategy, minimizing a defined "MigrationLoss" function. This function quantifies the discrepancy between the source and target environments, incorporating factors such as architectural differences, computational resource constraints, and operational dependencies. The theoretical framework suggests a potential pathway towards unifying critical areas within software engineering, namely cross-hardware compilation, software porting, and model deployment. The system iteratively explores potential transformation strategies, represented by a variable *T*, aiming to achieve the lowest possible MigrationLoss. This process leverages a search algorithm to discover the optimal transformation, offering a potentially scalable and robust solution for complex migration scenarios. The presented theory lays a foundational framework for future research and development in automated software migration.

title: Title: Computational Experience Explanation Theory (CEET)
abstract: Computational Experience Explanation Theory (CEET) proposes a systematic framework for answering the fundamental question: "Why did this experience arise?" CEET unifies three core concepts—experience, reasoning, and explanation—into a coherent computational architecture. Experience is represented as a high‑dimensional vector E = (e_1, e_2, ..., e_n) capturing observable data, internal states, and contextual cues. Reasoning is modelled as a transformation R = f(E) = (r_1, r_2, ..., r_m) that extracts latent causal relationships and inference paths from experience. Explanation is expressed as a symbolic or probabilistic narrative Exp = g(R) = (exp_1, exp_2, ..., exp_k) that translates reasoning into human‑interpretable accounts. The CEET pipeline leverages a layered architecture comprising data acquisition, feature extraction, probabilistic inference, causal modeling, and narrative synthesis. This paper details the mathematical formalism underlying each layer, presents algorithmic procedures for mapping experience to explanation, and discusses implications for artificial intelligence, cognitive science, and human‑computer interaction. The theory's potential to bridge experiential data and explanatory insight positions CEET as a candidate for high‑impact contributions, potentially meriting recognition such as a Turing Award.

title: Computational Rule Evolution Theory (CRET)
abstract: Computational Rule Evolution Theory (CRET) proposes a novel framework in which computational rules are treated as dynamic entities that undergo processes analogous to biological evolution. Unlike classical static logic or algorithmic systems, CRET allows a rule set R to transform over time according to a transition operator R_t → R_{t+1}. The theory formalizes mutation, selection, and recombination mechanisms within a rule space and introduces a differential equation model for the frequency of individual rule components. By mapping rule sets onto a fitness landscape, CRET captures how adaptive pressures steer rule evolution, leading to increasingly efficient or specialized computational behaviors. Illustrative examples include Boolean rule evolution, grid‑world navigation, and adaptive control of physical systems. The implications for self‑evolving software are profound: software can be conceived as a living system of rules that autonomously refines its own architecture, potentially yielding new classes of autonomic, self‑repairing, or self‑optimizing programs. CRET opens pathways toward a self‑evolving software theory, with the potential to contribute to the next generation of adaptive computing systems and to the broader field of artificial life.

title: Prior-art Note v1.0
abstract: Prior-art Note v1.0 is a companion document to Method Definition v1.0 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21931565). It documents the prior-art boundary of the defined practical AI-learning method by distinguishing established pedagogical and AI-tutoring mechanisms from the specific six-function method configuration fixed in the Method Definition. The Note reviews representative historical and contemporary precedents, including intelligent tutoring systems, instruction-programmed LLM tutors, learner-steering approaches, evidence-based checking and remediation, and transfer. It does not claim worldwide novelty or the absence of undocumented earlier implementations. The central finding is a bounded non-finding, assigned moderate rather than high confidence: within the reviewed public source set, no single documented precedent was identified that established all six mandatory functions together with the same allocation of control and the Minimal Profile defined in Method Definition v1.0. The deposit contains the canonical English version and an authorized Russian translation in both PDF and Markdown formats, together with SHA-256 checksums.

title: Towards a theory of inference-time alignment with unknown rewards
abstract: Generative model alignment has received broad interest, and significant progress has been made in supervised fine-tuning and inference-time computation. Yet, alignment has remained poorly understood from a statistical learning perspective. We formulate inference-time alignment as a weak-to-strong learning problem, where a reference policy (weak model) is assumed to be fairly good and the goal is to produce a strong model that predicts a good response at test time with arbitrarily high probability. Our problem is formulated as learning from scratch --- everything is learned from data rather than assuming access to a good reward estimate, and thus differs from the existing inference-time alignment theory. Our framework shares similarity to the recent work of Joshi et al., (arXiv:2510.15464), where for each prompt, there could be multiple good responses. Our definition of the alignment learnability follows the standard PAC learning principle. The core of our learning procedure works by learning a pairwise comparator and then running a tournament over candidate responses. evidence.title: Towards a theory of inference-time alignment with unknown rewards
evidence.abstract: Generative model alignment has received broad interest, and significant progress has been made in supervised fine-tuning and inference-time computation. Yet, alignment has remained poorly understood from a statistical learning perspective. We formulate inference-time alignment as a weak-to-strong learning problem, where a reference policy (weak model) is assumed to be fairly good and the goal is to produce a strong model that predicts a good response at test time with arbitrarily high probability. Our problem is formulated as learning from scratch --- everything is learned from data rather than assuming access to a good reward estimate, and thus differs from the existing inference-time alignment theory. title: MA-CERD: A Gold Benchmark Dataset for Counterfactual Requirements and Evidence Change Reasoning in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: MA-CERD (Multi-Agent Constraint-and-Evidence Reasoning Dataset) is a Gold benchmark dataset for evaluating reasoning under counterfactual requirement and evidence changes in multi-agent systems. The release contains 1,000 adjudicated Gold records constructed from 100 base cases and atomic semantic interventions. Each record captures the required relation, handling decision, impact set, preservation set, and provenance required to assess whether a system responds correctly to a changed requirement or evidence condition while preserving unaffected elements. Gold construction combines three separated evidence layers: O1 explicit-rule evidence, O2 blind human semantic review with third-party adjudication of disagreements, and O3 deterministic simulator-based shadow execution. The final release includes schema definitions, data dictionaries, family-level splits, privacy checks, evaluation utilities, intended-use documentation, and SHA-256 integrity manifests. The benchmark is intended for research on requirements evolution, change-impact reasoning, evidence-aware decision support, multi-agent systems, and leakage-resistant evaluation. It does not constitute operational validation, certified simulator fidelity, deployment readiness, or real-world safety assurance.

title: Dual Verification Computing
abstract: Dual Verification Computing (DVC) proposes a novel framework for verifying computational systems, moving beyond traditional notions of correctness and focusing on the simultaneous satisfaction of both correctness and acceptability. The core principle of DVC rests on the requirement that any computational action must simultaneously satisfy two verification conditions: $V_1 = \text{Correctness}$ and $V_2 = \text{Acceptability}$. Only when both conditions are true can the action be considered valid and executed. This approach has the potential to significantly expand the scope of program verification, potentially leading to a new paradigm of computing centered around systems that are not only correct but also demonstrably acceptable to their intended users and contexts. This document outlines the foundational concepts of DVC, explores its implications for system design and verification, and suggests avenues for future research. ---

title: Volume 42: Neural Networks & Informational Constraints
abstract: ABSTRACT Neural networks—both biological and artificial—represent one of the most profound manifestations of informational organization in nature and technology. This volume presents a comprehensive analysis of neural networks through the lens of the ICQER (Informational Constraints Quantum Event Realism) framework, demonstrating that neurons, synapses, and network architectures function fundamentally as constraint-driven informational systems. By examining neural computation as constraint propagation and optimization, we reveal how learning, memory, adaptation, and emergent intelligence arise from the dynamic interplay of local and global informational constraints. The volume is structured across ten sections that systematically develop the ICQER perspective on neural networks. Beginning with foundational principles, we establish neurons and synapses as constraint nodes and channels, and network architectures as constraint topologies. The analysis then progresses through constraint propagation mechanisms, demonstrating how forward and backward information flow represent informational shaping and optimization processes. Learning is reinterpreted as constraint optimization, unifying supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement paradigms under a single ICQER framework. Biological neural networks are examined in depth, highlighting how plasticity, network topology, and temporal dynamics embody constraint modulation in living systems. The emergence of intelligence and cognition is explained as a system-level resolution of constraints into coherent informational patterns, with hierarchical constraint organization enabling complex, multilevel processing. Temporal dynamics—including oscillations, synchronization, and predictive coding—are presented as manifestations of time-dependent constraints that enable memory, anticipation, and adaptive behavior. The volume addresses practical applications through sections on optimization and constraint engineering, demonstrating how ICQER principles guide the design of robust, efficient, and adaptable neural systems. Hybrid networks and neuromorphic computing are explored as embodiments of constraint-driven computation across biological and artificial substrates. Finally, we identify key challenges and open questions, including multi-scale constraint interactions, the bridge between biological and artificial systems, and the minimal constraint requirements for emergent cognition and consciousness. This volume bridges neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and complex systems theory, providing both theoretical foundations and practical insights for understanding, designing, and optimizing neural networks across domains. The ICQER framework illuminates the underlying principles that unify diverse neural systems, offering a roadmap for future research in both natural and artificial intelligence.

title: Unified Computational Intuition Theory (UCIT)
abstract: The Unified Computational Intuition Theory (UCIT) proposes that a key component of intelligent behavior is the ability to form compressed high‑dimensional representations of complex structures and to make rapid judgments based on these representations. UCIT integrates empirical learning, pattern recognition, expert judgment, scientific insight, and creativity into a single theoretical framework. By formalizing the relationship between experience, compression, and structure, UCIT aims to provide a mathematical foundation for future artificial intelligence systems that can autonomously generate, modify, and discover computational rules. This paper presents the core concepts of UCIT, develops a formal model using plain‑text mathematical notation, discusses its potential to become a foundational theory in AI, and introduces twenty novel research directions that build upon the core idea of computational rule generation.

title: Computational Reality Model Generation Theory (CRMGT)
abstract: This paper introduces the Computational Reality Model Generation Theory (CRMGT), a novel framework for understanding how intelligent systems can autonomously create internal models of their environments. While traditional machine learning approaches emphasize passive pattern extraction from data, CRMGT proposes that an adaptive system should actively generate and refine a structured representation of reality that guides perception, reasoning, and action. The theory is formalized through a set of equations and algorithmic procedures that describe the transformation from sensory input to an evolving internal reality model. We discuss the theoretical foundations, propose a concrete implementation strategy, and explore the implications of CRMGT for the development of general artificial intelligence. The potential of this theory to contribute to the next generation of intelligent systems, and possibly to be recognized with the Turing Award, is also examined.

title: IMPLEMENTASI ALGORITMA INDOBERT DAN SMOTE PADA ANALISIS SENTIMEN MASYARAKAT TERHADAP PROGRAM MAKAN BERGIZI GRATIS
abstract: Penelitian ini mengkaji polaritas sentimen masyarakat di media sosial X (Twitter) terkait program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) yang diluncurkan oleh pemerintah. Permasalahan utama dalam analisis data media sosial rill adalah tingginya tingkat ketidakseimbangan kelas (imbalanced dataset) antara opini positif dan negatif yang dapat menurunkan akurasi model cerdas. Penelitian ini mengusulkan solusi berupa kombinasi model IndoBERT sebagai ekstraktor fitur, metode Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) untuk penyeimbangan data, dan Feed-Forward Neural Network (FFNN) sebagai klasifikasi akhir. Dataset dikumpulkan melalui teknik scraping dan dipra-labeli menggunakan InSet Lexicon menjadi dua kategori polaritas (biner), yaitu positif dan negatif. Hasil pengujian menggunakan Stratified Train-Test Split berasio 90:10 menunjukkan bahwa model yang diusulkan berhasil mencapai akurasi sebesar 80%. Temuan utama membuktikan bahwa penerapan SMOTE mampu meningkatkan sensitivitas model terhadap kelas minoritas (positif) pada representasi vektor IndoBERT.

title: The Distributional View of Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Token-level knowledge distillation (KD) matches two conditional distributions per position, yet the standard objectives compare them pointwise: a Kullback-Leibler gradient is blind to which wrong token receives probability mass. We develop a distributional view in which the teacher is represented not by a single softened output but by a family of multi-temperature views - marginals of the annealing path of its logits - and the student is trained against a geometry-aware aggregate of these views under an embedding-based ground cost. We formalize the resulting design space (mixtures, log-linear pooling, entropic Wasserstein barycenters, and a debiased Sinkhorn-divergence flagship in hub and path forms), prove an exact collapse result showing log-linear pooling of tempered views is equivalent to a single temperature, and give a multi-marginal Schrodinger-bridge reading that yields falsifiable predictions. On instruction-tuned Pythia pairs, experiments yield three empirical laws: (i) dispersion law - the benefit of multi-temperature aggregation grows monotonically with the effective temperature dispersion of the views, not with their number; (ii) dispersed views unlock the aggregation operator - the barycenter separates from the arithmetic mixture exactly when transport-based aggregation starts to beat averaging; and (iii) two-regime picture governed by the ceiling gap $Γ=\mathrm{PPL}_{\mathrm{SFT}}-\mathrm{PPL}_{T}$: when the fine-tuned teacher barely beats a supervised student the gentle transport objective is the best KD loss but no KD beats supervised fine-tuning, whereas at a real ceiling the ranking inverts - and the sign of the fidelity-generalization correlation flips. We argue that "which distillation loss is the best" is not a fixed property of the loss but a function of $Γ$.

title: Self-Reproducing Program Constraints: A Novel Approach to Software Security
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Self-Reproducing Program Constraints (SRPC) as a paradigm shift in software security. The core idea revolves around creating a system where constraints not only limit a program but also autonomously generate new constraints. This dynamic constraint generation is governed by a process that takes the previous constraint set (C_t) and a background state (B_t) as input, and produces a new constraint set (C_{t+1}). Crucially, the newly generated constraint (C_{t+1}) must be consistent with a predefined "safe" constraint set (C_safe). This iterative process aims to establish a self-adaptive security architecture, potentially unlocking new theoretical foundations for adaptive and resilient software systems. The approach leverages the inherent ability of programs to modify themselves, but directs this modification toward strengthening security rather than introducing vulnerabilities. We present a formal framework for SRPC, outlining the key components and operational rules, and discuss the theoretical implications and potential of this approach.

title: Program Behavior Phase Space (PBPS)
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Program Behavior Phase Space (PBPS), a novel framework for analyzing program behavior beyond traditional output-based evaluations. The core idea is that program execution represents a trajectory within a multi-dimensional phase space, where each dimension corresponds to a relevant observable state of the program. This approach allows for the identification of regions of stability, chaotic behavior, and transition boundaries within the program's execution dynamics. We explore the potential of PBPS to provide a more nuanced and mathematically rigorous understanding of program behavior, with implications for areas such as software verification, program optimization, and the study of complex systems. The framework offers a potential route towards developing new analytical tools and mathematical models for program analysis, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of how programs behave.

title: Computational Identity Generation Theory (CIGT): A Unified Framework for Artificial Identity
abstract: Identity is a fundamental construct in both natural and artificial systems. Traditional approaches to artificial identity have largely focused on either symbolic rule‑based methods or deep neural networks, each capturing only a fragment of the multifaceted process by which an entity forms a coherent self‑representation. Computational Identity Generation Theory (CIGT) proposes a concise yet comprehensive model that captures the dynamic interplay between Structure, Memory, and Goal as the core drivers of identity formation. The theory is expressed in the simple functional form I = f(S, M, G), where I denotes the identity state, S the structural schema, M the accumulated memory traces, and G the set of goals guiding interpretation and action. By formalizing identity as the result of continuous interaction among these three components, CIGT offers a unified lens for understanding artificial life, social robotics, and adaptive systems. The present paper develops the theoretical foundations, outlines computational instantiations, and discusses the implications of CIGT for the future of autonomous agents and the potential for recognition at the level of the Turing Award.

title: Computational Rule Fusion Theory (CRFT)
abstract: Computational Rule Fusion Theory (CRFT) proposes a systematic framework for combining elementary computational rules to create novel computational mechanisms. By treating rules as modular, composable units, CRFT formalizes the operation R1 + R2 → R3 as a rule‑fusion transformation that expands the expressiveness of a given computational system. The theory establishes closure properties, identifies sufficient conditions for fusion to produce well‑defined functions, and demonstrates how iterative application of fusion can generate complex algorithms automatically. We illustrate CRFT with concrete examples from arithmetic, string manipulation, and graph traversal, and discuss its implications for algorithm design, automated code generation, and the theoretical foundations of computation. The potential of CRFT to enable autonomous algorithm discovery positions it as a candidate for transformative impact in computer science, warranting recognition at the level of a Turing Award.

title: Computational Reality Model Singularity Theory (CRMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel theoretical framework called Computational Reality Model Singularity Theory (CRMS). CRMS posits that a system capable of generating progressively more accurate and internally consistent models of reality can trigger a self‑amplifying cycle of model refinement, leading to a singularity point where model fidelity surpasses the system's own experiential limits. We formalize the recursive enhancement process, analyze the conditions under which a singularity emerges, and discuss potential implications for the emergence of superintelligent agents. The theory integrates concepts from formal modeling, epistemic logic, and computational complexity, and offers a deterministic lens through which to examine the trajectory of intelligence amplification.

title: Implementasi Algoritma Naïve Bayes dan Decision Tree pada Sentimen Dampak Bencana Hidrometoeorologi
abstract: Bencana hidrometeorologi memicu berbagai respons masyarakat di media sosial. maka diperlukan analisis untuk memahami opini publik terhadap bencana terkait. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah membandingkan kinerja algoritma Naïve Bayes dan Decision Tree dalam melakukan analisis sentimen terkait bencana Hidrometeorologi. Data digunakan berasal dari TikTok, Instagram Facebook yang terdiri dari 11.890 komentar dengan label kelas positif, negatif, dan netral yang kemudian diproses melalui tahapan pra-pemrosesan, pembobotan TF-IDF, dan klasifikasi dan validasi 5-fold cross validation. Hasil validasi menunjukkan Naïve Bayes memperoleh mean accuracy 0,79 lebih tinggi daripada Decision Tree yang mendapat skor 0,65. Pada data uji, Naïve Bayes memperoleh accuracy, precision, recall, dan F1-Score yang seragam 0,79 lebih unggul dari Decision Tree dengan accuracy 0,63, precision 0,70, recall 0,63, dan F1-score 0,64. Dikarenakan jarak mean acmecuracy dan test accuracy berdekatan disimpulkan Naïve Bayes mempunyai kemampuan generalisasi lebih baik daripada Decision Tree. Hasil ini menunjukkan Naïve Bayes unggul dalam mengklasifikasi sentimen terkait bencana Hidrometeorologi

evidence.title: Implementasi Algoritma Naïve Bayes dan Decision Tree pada Sentimen Dampak Bencana Hidrometoeorologi
evidence.abstract: Bencana hidrometeorologi memicu berbagai respons masyarakat di media sosial. maka diperlukan analisis untuk memahami opini publik terhadap bencana terkait. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah membandingkan kinerja algoritma Naïve Bayes dan Decision Tree dalam melakukan analisis sentimen terkait bencana Hidrometeorologi. Data digunakan berasal dari TikTok, Instagram Facebook yang terdiri dari 11.890 komentar dengan label kelas positif, negatif, dan netral yang kemudian diproses melalui tahapan pra-pemrosesan, pembobotan TF-IDF, dan klasifikasi dan validasi 5-fold cross validation. Hasil validasi menunjukkan Naïve Bayes memperoleh mean accuracy 0,79 lebih tinggi daripada Decision Tree yang mendapat skor 0,65. Pada data uji, Naïve Bayes memperoleh accuracy, precision, recall, dan F1-Score yang seragam 0,79 lebih unggul dari Decision Tree dengan accuracy 0,63, precision 0,70, recall 0,63, dan F1-score 0,64. Dikarenakan jarak mean acmecuracy dan test accuracy berdekatan disimpulkan Naïve Bayes mempunyai kemampuan generalisasi lebih baik daripada Decision Tree. Hasil ini menunjukkan Naïve Bayes unggul dalam mengklasifikasi sentimen terkait bencana Hidrometeorologi

title: TAHB: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Text-Attributed Hypergraph Learning
abstract: Hypergraphs effectively model higher-order groupwise relationships beyond pairwise interactions, while pretrained language models (PLMs) and large language models (LLMs) provide rich semantic understanding from textual attributes. However, research on combining language models with hypergraph learning remains limited due to the lack of public text-attributed hypergraph benchmarks. To address this limitation, we present TAHB (Text-Attributed Hypergraph Benchmark), the first public benchmark integrating hypergraph structures and raw textual attributes. TAHB contains 10 real-world datasets from four domains - e-commerce, academia, movies, and politics networks - enabling systematic evaluation of text-aware hypergraph representation learning. Experimental results show that TAHB preserves key structural properties of real-world hypergraphs and consistently reproduces performance tendencies observed in existing benchmarks. Furthermore, experiments under both LLM-as-Enhancer and LLM-as-Predictor settings demonstrate that LLM-enhanced textual semantics improve hypergraph learning performance, while structural and textual information jointly provide the best setting for LLM-based prediction. Our benchmark provides a foundation for future research at the intersection of hypergraph learning and language models.

title: 认知因果学:面向跨载体智慧体的因果拓扑畸变诊断与校准框架 Causal-Cognitive Science: A Diagnostic and Calibration Framework for Causal-Topological Distortions Across Substrate-Independent Intelligences
abstract: 作者:郭洋洋Author: Guo YangyangORCID:0009-0006-6669-1790通讯邮箱:gyy-goes@foxmail.com发布类型:预印本Publication Type: Preprint提交日期:2026 年 8 月 15 日Submission Date: August 15, 2026版本:v1.0 中英双语定稿版Version: v1.0 Final Bilingual Edition预印本 DOI:10.5281/zenodo.21948408Preprint DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21948408开源协议:CC BY 4.0Open Access License: CC BY 4.0 摘要 Abstract 人类个体在推理与决策中普遍存在因果谬误与认知偏差,大规模语言模型在生成过程中普遍出现事实编造与逻辑跳步,这两类现象长期被分置在心理学与人工智能两个互不往来的研究传统中。本文提出一门构想中的通用学科——认知因果学,将研究对象从碳基人类个体拓展至一切具备因果建模能力的智慧体,包含硅基人工智能系统。本文将认知幻觉重新定义为智慧体内部因果拓扑映射畸变的外在显现,并提出五条跨载体通用的研究公理:智能建模公理、畸变内生公理、幻觉同源公理、结构可诊公理与校准可迁公理。在此基础上,本文归纳虚假因果关联、概念拓扑畸变、因果时序倒置、推理链路断裂、基准锚定畸变五种典型畸变模式,给出碳基与硅基表现的同构对照;建立包含输入观测、层级定位与来源鉴别的诊断流程;提出分层校准、元认知反射、有限校准目标与跨载体迁移边界四项通用校准原则;并给出三条理论假设与三条可实证检验的假设。本文属于理论范式构想,所提假设均有待后续实验验证,公理体系为学科预设前提而非已被证实的经验定律。 Causal fallacies and cognitive biases are pervasive in human reasoning and decision-making, while large language models routinely produce factual fabrications and logical leaps during generation. These two classes of phenomena have long been confined to two non-communicating research traditions: psychology and artificial intelligence. This paper proposes a conceived general discipline — Causal-Cognitive Science — that extends its research object from carbon-based human individuals to all intelligences capable of causal modeling, including silicon-based artificial intelligence systems. Cognitive hallucination is redefined as the outward manifestation of distortions in an intelligence's internal causal-topological mapping. Five substrate-independent research axioms are proposed: the Axiom of Intelligent Modeling, the Axiom of Endogenous Distortion, the Axiom of Homologous Hallucination, the Axiom of Structural Diagnosability, and the Axiom of Transferable Calibration. On this basis, five typical distortion patterns are identified — spurious causal association, conceptual-topological distortion, reversed causal order, broken reasoning chain, and baseline anchoring distortion — with isomorphic comparisons between carbon-based and silicon-based manifestations. A diagnostic workflow comprising input observation, hierarchical localization, and source identification is established. Four general calibration principles are proposed: layered calibration, metacognitive reflection, finite calibration targets, and cross-substrate migration boundaries. Three theoretical hypotheses and three empirically testable hypotheses are presented. This paper is a theoretical paradigm proposal; all hypotheses await subsequent experimental verification, and the axiomatic system serves as a disciplinary presupposition rather than an empirically confirmed law. 关键词:认知因果学;因果拓扑畸变;认知幻觉;跨载体智能;元认知校准 Keywords: Causal-Cognitive Science; causal-topological distortion; cognitive hallucination; substrate-independent intelligence; metacognitive calibration

title: Computational Capability Search Theory (CCST-2)
abstract: This paper introduces Computational Capability Search Theory (CCST-2), a novel framework designed to address the escalating demand for enhanced computational capabilities within artificial intelligence and scientific computing. The core concept revolves around a system's proactive search for novel capabilities, rather than relying solely on pre-defined or static architectures. This theory proposes a systematic approach to identifying and integrating untapped computational resources, potentially unlocking significant advancements in machine learning, optimization, and simulation. The theory utilizes a search function, `Search(NewCapability)`, which represents the iterative process of identifying, evaluating, and integrating these new computational resources. The potential impact of CCST-2 is substantial, suggesting a pathway towards fundamental breakthroughs in computer science and the development of truly intelligent machines. The theory is presented here without experimental validation, focusing instead on the theoretical underpinnings and potential applications. ---
